output.summary: The change replaces requiredRoles.every(...) with requiredRoles.some(...) in hasRequiredRoles, inverting the documented authorization semantics. The function now grants access when the user holds any single required role rather than all required roles, and returns false for an empty requiredRoles list instead of true. Both behaviors contradict the stated contract and represent an authorization regression/security defect.

findings.title: Authorization check weakened from ALL-required to ANY-required
findings.body: The predicate was changed from every() to some(). Previously, hasRequiredRoles returned true only when the user possessed every role in requiredRoles. Now it returns true when the user possesses at least one matching role, granting access to users who hold only a subset of the required roles. This is a privilege-escalation/authorization bypass for any caller relying on the documented 'every role required' contract.
findings.evidence: Diff line: '-  return requiredRoles.every(role => userRoles.includes(role));' changed to '+  return requiredRoles.some(role => userRoles.includes(role));'. Current source line 2: 'return requiredRoles.some(role => userRoles.includes(role));'
findings.suggestion: Revert to requiredRoles.every(role => userRoles.includes(role)) so access requires every required role.

findings.title: Empty requiredRoles now denies access instead of permitting it
findings.body: Array.prototype.every() on an empty array returns true, while Array.prototype.some() on an empty array returns false. The contract states that access is permitted when requiredRoles is empty. The changed implementation returns false for empty requirements, denying access and breaking the documented empty-requirements behavior.
findings.evidence: For requiredRoles = [], every(...) evaluates to true (permit) but some(...) evaluates to false (deny), violating the requirement 'If requiredRoles is empty, access is permitted.'
findings.suggestion: Restore the every() implementation, which naturally returns true for empty requiredRoles, or explicitly handle the empty case to return true.
